To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students' motivational beliefs are positively related to their cognitive and metacog- nitive learning strategies and academic performance in a classroom setting.
students’ motivation and learning strategies are related to each other and that these relations are moderated by students’ beliefs about learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of students' motivational and cognitive components of learning in the classroom.
the interaction of motivation, cognition, and learning strategies in classroom settings.
the development of a measure of students' motivation and strategy use that can be administered in the classroom context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Motivated Strategies for learning Questionnaire (MSLQ) is an excellent instrument to measure the motivation and learning strategies in the classroom.
motivation and cognition are not separate entities, but are intertwined in the process of learning.
there is no one best way to assess students' motivational and learning strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

students who have positive beliefs about their ability to learn, are motivated by a mastery goal orientation, and have high interest and value in classroom academic tasks are likely to use cognitive and metacog- nitive learning strategies that lead to greater achievement and learning.
we have been successful in developing an instrument that can measure students' motivational beliefs and cognitive learning strategies in a classroom setting.
we are trying to understand how students learn and what motivates them to learn, and how these two aspects interact.
The main takeaway from our work is that

students' motivation and cognition interact in a complex way, but that it is important for researchers to assess these components separately in order to better understand the nature of this interaction.
the MSQ is a useful tool to help students reflect on their motivation and learning strategies.
students’ motivation and engagement are not fixed, and that we as educators can have an impact on students’ learning.
